plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for Viprinet router. It reports uptime, CPU utilization, memory used, temperature, fan, power supply status, and interface traffic (enterprise PEN 35424).
name: Router

metrics.name: device_cpu_load
metrics.description: CPU load average of the Viprinet router (vpnRouterCPULoad). This is a parsed load-average string, not a utilization percentage. Unparseable values are dropped.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes, measured in bytes per second, from the 64-bit IF-MIB ifHCInOctets counter (ifXTable).

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric calculates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, measured in bytes per second, from the 64-bit IF-MIB ifHCOutOctets counter (ifXTable).

metrics.name: device_memory_used
metrics.description: Used memory of the Viprinet router in bytes (vpnRouterMemoryUsage, reported in KB and converted to bytes). The MIB does not expose total, free, or utilization percentage.

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: Chassis temperature of the Viprinet router in degrees Celsius. System temperature is the primary reading; CPU temperature is collected as a second sensor. The dashboard takes the maximum per instance.

metrics.name: device_psu_state
metrics.description: Power-supply health of the Viprinet router, normalized from vpnRouterPowerSupplyFailure so that 0 (no failure) becomes 1 (normal) and 1 (failure) becomes 2 (abnormal).

metrics.name: device_fan_state
metrics.description: Fan operative status of the Viprinet router. Raw codes 0=Disabled, 1=OK, 2=Faulty are normalized so that 1 remains healthy and every other code is abnormal.

metrics.name: device_fan_speed
metrics.description: Current fan RPM of the Viprinet router. Not all models supply this value.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
